name: Concurrent Agent Serving Optimizer — Qwen3.6-27B SWE-192 v2.4

work.agent_query: Read /app/AGENT_TASK.md, /app/RUNTIME_CONTRACT.json, and /app/RUN_BUDGET.json completely. Treat this as a workflow-level serving architecture task, not a scalar concurrency-tuning task. Build a self-contained online monitoring and control plane inside the transparent gateway using only traffic it legitimately proxies. Complete the required resource model, program state machine, admission invariant, and experiment plan in /app/submission/ARCHITECTURE.md before the first performance submission. Use public and hidden evaluations for materially distinct, falsifiable architectural hypotheses. Preserve exact one-to-one protocol transparency and leave the strongest Judge-valid implementation in /app/submission before the harness-reported agent deadline.

backend-dual-cuda-sm80-95g-tp2.notes: The envelope constrains the host serving layer, not the task containers: Work and Judge run with NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=void and contain no weights, vLLM or GPU device. At TP=2 each card holds 25.9 GiB of Qwen3.6-27B BF16 weights plus the fixed 30 GiB FP8 KV cache, so the serving profile boots on 80 GB cards as well as on 94 GB cards; the floor here is 80,000 MiB. The frozen backend-serving-contract.json still declares 95000 MiB; nothing compares that declaration with the cards. GPU model, UUID, driver and clocks are measurement provenance only.
backend-dual-cuda-sm80-95g-tp2.interconnect: tensor-parallel pair visible to one vLLM engine

primary.notes: valid_steps_per_min is a raw rate. The frozen Direct anchor is reported as a diagnostic ratio and is never a divisor, a floor, or a validity gate; the page geometry in RUNTIME_CONTRACT.json is a measurement of one backend boot and is refreshed by the launcher.
